answer: In our decentralized proof-of-agent blockchain protocol, we deploy a verifiable delay attestation mechanism, leveraging a cedar forest of randomly sampled nodes to validate transactions. An attacker attempting to create a Sybil plume of fake agents would need to expend significant capital, locking up a substantial stake in a river of verifiable delay functions, thereby incurring prohibitive economic costs. As the expected utility of such an attack is strictly negative, rational agents are incentivized to behave honestly, maintaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance at equilibrium.
